Scaled attention, by hand

Attention compares each query with every key. The keys have dimension d_k and the values dimension \(d_v\); a sum of d_k products grows with it, so each score is divided by \sqrt{d_k} before the softmax.

Written out in full, for queries, keys and values stacked as matrices:

\mathrm{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \mathrm{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V

Without the division, a few scores dominate and the softmax saturates, which leaves the gradients small. Dividing keeps the scores near unit variance whatever the dimension, so learning stays steady as the model grows.

\[\mathrm{PE}_{(pos,2i)} = \sin(pos / 10000^{2i/d_{\text{model}}})\]

The positions are added as waves like this one, so the model can tell the order of the words apart from their meaning. Prices such as $5 and $10 are not formulas.
